toolProblems: javascript_tool silently corrupts long string literals containing repeated character runs: a 19,644-char base64 JPEG arrived 1,071 chars short, and a retry lost 284 bytes. The first corruption was discovered only AFTER upload, creating one unintended Asset. Mitigation used thereafter: gzip the file (high entropy, no runs), base64 it, split into ≤5,568-char chunks with in-page length verification, decompress via DecompressionStream, and hash-guard before dispatch — abort on mismatch. All later uploads matched byte-exactly.

The Browser pane was hidden for part of the run, so coordinate clicks failed with 'not compositing frames' and tabs_select did not help; non-spending product controls ('Use whole video', 'Cancel') were activated via their own button elements. No spending control was ever activated this way.

Page CSP blocks connect-src beyond the app origin: a localhost helper fetch failed, and the product's own media URL cannot be fetched because it redirects cross-origin to object storage (opaqueredirect) — this is what prevented the byte-for-byte download comparison in REAL-12.

The in-app Browser has no file_upload tool, so uploads were injected into the product's own hidden file input via DataTransfer; the upload still runs the product's real client action chain (uploadFilesDirect -> authorizeUpload -> finalize), only the OS file picker is bypassed.

Deploy-time upload failure with misleading copy (merchant-visible defect): after a redeploy, an already-open page's server actions return 404 and EVERY upload from that page fails with 'Reference couldn't be attached — We couldn't upload that file. Check your connection and try again.' Confirmed by instrumenting fetch (two POSTs to the page route, both 404, no storage request attempted) and by cure-by-reload: identical bytes that failed repeatedly uploaded first try on a freshly loaded page. The copy blames the merchant's connection for a deploy-side condition and cost ~25 minutes of misdiagnosis (I first believed video upload was broken). Suggest detecting the stale-action 404 and prompting a reload.
